newsitem.title: GERMANY: German debt and futures under pressure from France.
newsitem.headline: German debt and futures under pressure from France.

text.p: German Bunds and futures were under pressure in early dealings on Monday after French left-wing parties unexpectedly outpolled ruling centre-right coalition in the first round of voting in French elections.

A weaker dollar, tied to the French election results, and national holidays in Britain and the United States also weighed on the market in thin dealings as losses in French debt markets spread to neighbouring countries.
German DTB June Bund futures fell 19 basis points at 100.76 but were off a low at 100.70. The benchmark 10-year Bund due July 2007 was at 100.54 points, down from 100.79 on Friday.

Traders said the French election results would likely only have a short-term impact on the German market and looked for June futures to remain within a range from 100.60 to 101.00 points during the rest of the week.

"We are holding up relatively well considering the election," said one Frankfurt trader. "The French have already signed off on currency union, so the impact of a Socialist victory in the end would not be overly worrisome."
The market showed little reaction to the state of Hesse reporting a 0.1 percent month-on-month rise in consumer prices, slightly lower than other state CPI reports issued last week.
The provisional state reports are leading the market to expect west German consumer prices for May to rise about 0.4 percent month-on-month and 1.4 percent for the year.
While the upward trend in May inflation gave the market a jolt, traders said it did not hurt long-term sentiment.
On a technical basis, MMS International said the opening gap in June Bund futures from 100.95 to 100.80 has put moderate support at 100.57 and 100.45 and further support at 100.20.
"This is the level for long-term bears to break," MMS said of the 100.20 level for June futures. "Any upticks are limited to attempting to fill the gap but this looks ambitious..."
